messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: 5xx and p99 timeout surge detected for /v1/generate in us-west-2. Error rate > 3% for last 5m, paging sre-oncall :rotating_light:

sre-oncall: Acked. I’m on it — jumping into dashboards and logs.

maya: Seeing cluster-wide connection timeouts from the runtime pool. p95 -> 1.2s, p99 -> 6.8s on the new canary. First noticed ~2m after the deploy.

alex: Confirmed. Rolling deploy v2026-03-17-77 was pushed 00:02 UTC. Traces show early `upstream timeout` 502s and `connection reset` from gpu-host-07. Snip from logs:
```
[03/17/2026 00:05:12] GET /v1/generate 502 upstream timeout id=abc123 host=gpu-host-07 latency=0.420s
[03/17/2026 00:05:13] GET /v1/generate 504 connection reset id=abc124 host=gpu-host-07 latency=6.754s
```

tess: Customer-impact: internal SLO alerts triggered; we’re seeing error spikes for a handful of enterprise tenants (high-throughput). Customer-success, heads-up so we can pre-emptively notify if this persists.

customer-success: Copy. Preparing holding message template. Will update if impact broadens.

ryan: Quick triage — is it a model weight load or runtime change? Any correlating infra changes?

alex: The canary included an updated kernel flag and a runtime NVTX patch. Host telemetry shows increased TCP retransmits on gpu-host-07..10. Also the `keepalive` window seems to be smaller on the new kernel.

maya: I’m switching the canary traffic to the previous variant (v2026-03-17-76) via route override to stop customer impact and buy time for deeper debug.

sre-oncall: Please do that, and also scale up fallback pool to soak incoming. Execute: `redwood route set --service generate --variant v2026-03-17-76 --percent 100`

alex: Running rollback command now: `./deploy rollback --service=generate --id=v2026-03-17-77`

incident-bot: ACTION: Rollback initiated by alex at 00:06 UTC. Canary traffic diverted.

maya: Metrics updating — error rate dropping in the next scrape. p99 trending down to 0.9s, errors falling toward baseline.

sre-oncall: Great. Keep the rollback pinned until we confirm host-level kernel interaction. Assigning follow-up: alex (runtime) and maya (serving) to dig into kernel flag + NVTX patch.

alex: Will capture host tcpdump and kernel logs, and reproduce on a staging pool. Suspect: keepalive and kernel timers causing premature stream closes under sustained kv-cache pressure.

tess: Noting customer-impact: a handful of high-traffic enterprise customers saw degraded throughput for ~3-6 minutes; no persistent data loss. CS will send an update: "short service disruption during deploy; rollback applied; investigating root cause"

customer-success: Draft ready, sending once you confirm final status.

maya: Postmortem checklist: preserve canary hosts, collect nvram/kernel configs, and snapshot network stats. Also notify infra to hold similar kernel flips until regression window passes.

sre-oncall: Will hand off to the next on-call at 00:20 UTC. If anyone else sees a new spike after rollback, page immediately.

ryan: FYI I’ll open a tracking issue with the rollout metadata and add the playbook link: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/deploy-timeout-regression

alex: Attaching initial artifacts in the issue: tcpdump, dmesg, deploy manifest.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated — rollback applied, error rate returning to baseline. Monitoring for 30m.

sre-oncall: Closing active pager. Handoff: @maya owns follow-up RCA, @alex reproduces in staging, @tess coordinates customer comms.

maya: Acknowledged. I’ll post a short RCA draft in #postmortems once we have kernel confirmation.

customer-success: Thanks team — we’ll standby for the customer note. :thumbsup:
